question.text: What are the risk factors a Regulated Entity must consider while conducting a Business Risk Assessment under the IFSCA Guidelines?

answer.text: Type of customers and activities; countries or geographic areas; products, services, delivery channels and activity profiles; complexity and volume of transactions; new products and business practices; and use of new or developing technologies
Type of customers and their activities, and countries or geographic areas of engagement
Products, services, delivery channels, and the complexity and volume of transactions
Development of new products and use of new or developing technologies

explanation.text: The Logic: The Business Risk Assessment must consider, to the extent applicable and relevant: (i) type of customers and activities; (ii) countries or geographic areas; (iii) products, services, delivery channels and activity profiles; (iv) complexity and volume of transactions; (v) development of new products and business practices; and (vi) use of new or developing technologies. The correct answer encompasses all six factors. The Trap: The distractors each cite a real subset of the factors (customer/geography, products/channels, or new products/technologies), so a candidate who recognises any one item could be tempted to stop there. The IFSCA Guidelines require all six factors to be considered together as part of a single business risk assessment. Note: Replaced the answer-randomization-fragile 'All of the above' wording with a standalone comprehensive option that lists the factors, and removed the cross-exam/pro-tip lines that were not source-grounded.
